# Heatmap Tracker

> A free, open-source Obsidian plugin that turns any dated note into an interactive,
> GitHub-style heatmap. Track habits, workouts, mood, sleep, finances, reading and work
> logs from frontmatter already in your vault. All computation is local — no account,
> no sync, no telemetry. Apache-2.0.

Install: https://obsidian.md/plugins?id=heatmap-tracker
Source: https://github.com/mokkiebear/heatmap-tracker

## How it works

- Add a frontmatter value to a dated note, e.g. `steps: 8420`. Booleans count as 1.
- Recommended: run the **Insert Heatmap Tracker** command (or click the ribbon icon) and
  fill in the modal — it has a live preview, tells you how many notes match, and writes
  the codeblock for you. Every rendered heatmap carries an edit button that reopens the
  same form and rewrites its codeblock.
- Or write the `heatmap-tracker` codeblock yourself with `property: steps`. Optional keys:
  `path`, `tags`, `filters` (`equals`, `contains`, `notEmpty`).
- Or call `renderHeatmapTracker(container, trackerData)` from a `dataviewjs` block for
  full control over the dataset.
- The `heatmap-tracker` codeblock requires the Dataview plugin; the JavaScript API does not.

## Capabilities

- Guided create/edit modal with a live preview and match count; no YAML required.
- Yearly contribution grid or a monthly calendar layout (`layout: "monthly"`).
- Flexible ranges: `monthsToShow`, `daysToShow`, or `startDate` + `endDate`.
- Color palettes in settings, `colorScheme.customColors` per heatmap, `customColor` per entry.
- Intensity scaling via `intensityConfig.scaleStart` / `scaleEnd`.
- Statistics tab with totals, streaks and user-defined `insights`.
- Export tab: a report as Markdown or self-contained HTML, with the grid, a labelled
  legend, a summary line and each day's note content grouped by week.
- Click a square to open the note behind it, or create it (`disableFileCreation: false`).
- 9 UI languages; desktop and mobile.
